title: remote: guard against future timestamps
body:
As described in #19864 - future-dated exemplars advance sent timestamps without advancing received timestamps. 

Currently this will produce negative numbers in desired shards calculation and resulting in remote-write shards scaling down to 1. Future sent timestamps can also advance the Agent WAL truncation cutoff beyond recent samples - truncating data that was not yet sent.

In this PR:

- Clamp negative backlog estimates to zero when sizing shards.
- Cap the Agent WAL cutoff at `now - MinWALTime`, preserving the maximum-retention bound.
- Add focused tests for the changes.
- Add a comment explaining why exemplar timestamps are not used to advance received timestamps

#### Which issue(s) does the PR fix:

Fixes #19864

#### Release notes for end users

```release-notes
[BUGFIX] Remote write: Prevent future-dated exemplars from scaling shards down to the minimum.
[BUGFIX] Agent: Prevent future sent timestamps from advancing WAL truncation beyond the minimum retention window.
```

files.patch:
@@ -1174,7 +1174,7 @@ func (t *QueueManager) calculateDesiredShards() int {
 		dataPendingRate = dataInRate*dataKeptRatio - dataOutRate
 		highestSent     = t.metrics.highestSentTimestamp.Get()
 		highestRecv     = t.highestRecvTimestamp.Get()
-		delay           = highestRecv - highestSent
+		delay           = max(highestRecv-highestSent, 0) // Delay must never be negative.
 		dataPending     = delay * dataInRate * dataKeptRatio
 	)

-	require.Equal(t, before+2, prom_testutil.ToFloat64(exemplarsIn))
